alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare English imperative.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *them* and nothing else; the relativizer stays with the participle.

Attributive participle recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer *that* and the auxiliary *had* are rule 7/9 helpers on the participle. Rule 17 heads the support-verb rendering *had the rule* on the meaning-bearing complement *rule*, not on the finite *had*.

Genitive complement of the participle: *over* realizes the bare case and rides with the pronoun, no Greek preposition being expressed and no article standing to anchor it, exactly as at HEB.13.7, HEB.13.17 and HEB.13.24 alike. 2CO.11.2 `ὑμᾶς` → *over you* reads a bare case the same way unhedged, and 2CO.1.24 is the same support-verb shape — `κυριεύομεν` → *we have lordship* with `πίστεως` → *over faith* — though hedged and conceding the other reading. That other reading is live and the corpus does not settle it: 1PE.5.3 `κατακυριεύοντες` → *lording it over* keeps *over* inside the verb's unit unhedged, and the corpus generally keeps a bare-case particle on an English phrasal verb, as `ἀνέχομαι` → *bear with* does in four units and as this chapter's own HEB.13.22 and HEB.13.14 *we seek after* do. I take the complement here because `ἡγέομαι` has no corpus unit of its own to follow and the nearest same-shape precedent is 2CO.1.24's *have + noun + over*, where the English preposition heads a phrase expressing the people ruled rather than being a particle the verb selects; reading it as the idiom's own particle remains defensible.

Relative pronoun expanded with a supplied generic antecedent noun. Rule 77 heads such a unit on the generic noun (*the things which* → *things*), so the head is *men*; heading on the relativizer *that*, as for a bare antecedent, remains defensible.
Aorist indicative; the relativizer belongs to the relative pronoun's unit.
Dative pronoun; the case preposition *unto* rides with it under rule 21, no article being present.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article.
The ASV gives *God* no determiner, so the article has no *the* to anchor: rule 21's determinerless clause makes it `unrepresented` under rule 23 and leaves the case preposition with the noun.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*; rule 17 heads it on the noun.

Asyndetic seam between two coordinate imperative clauses, both rendered alike, with no Greek conjunction anywhere in the verse: rule 98 makes the supplied juncture `added` under rule 5. Rule 88 does not reach it, being scoped to a circumstantial participle converted into a coordinate finite clause, and the participle here stays a participle.
Circumstantial participle rendered by the English participle.
Genitive relative pronoun rendered by the possessive *their*, which is what displaces the following article's determiner under rule 20.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19.
Noun stands alone.
Rule 20 displacement: the genitive `ὧν` already occupies the English determiner slot with *their*, so this article realizes nothing and *of* stays with its noun.
Discontinuous under rule 15, the intervening *their* belonging to `ὧν`. The ASV renders `ἀναστροφή` here by a bare *life*; where it writes *manner of life* rule 66 heads that phrase on *life* too.
Imperative rendered by the bare English imperative.

Rule 76: the only candidate possessor, `ὧν`, has already been spent on the earlier *their* of *their life*, so it is not available here and the article itself takes the supplied possessive, as rules 51 and 60 have it for a supplied indefinite or demonstrative.
Noun stands bare, its determiner having gone to the article.

review_notes: Both articles of `τοῦ θεοῦ` and `τῆς ἀναστροφῆς` are `unrepresented` for different reasons: the first because the ASV supplies no determiner at all (rules 21/23), the second because `ὧν` occupies the slot (rule 20).
The verse-medial *and* is the only `added` unit; a reference comparison keyed to rule 88 would report it as a disagreement, but rule 98's asyndetic-seam case governs here.
